samples.summary: The GIT_* scrubbing added by this change lives only in the test file; the production module it protects still spawns git with an inherited environment
samples.evidence: scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs:50 deletes every `GIT_*` var from `process.env` at module scope, and its comment explains the hazard: git exports `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE` to hooks, and `verify:self` runs from `pre-push`. But the module under test is unchanged: `scripts/changed-areas.mjs:255` (`resolveRefs`'s `git()` helper) and `scripts/changed-areas.mjs:350` (`git diff --name-only ${base}...${head}`) call `execFileSync("git", …, { cwd: repoRoot })` with **no `env`**, so under a hook they answer about whatever `GIT_DIR` names, not `repoRoot`. `scripts/verify-self.mjs:8` imports those very functions and is the pre-push entry point (it is careful enough to read HEAD via `readHeadSha`, see verify-self.mjs:543-547). The repo already ships the canonical fix — `repoScopedEnv()` / `fixtureGitEnv()` in scripts/agent/git-env.mjs:102,120 — and neither changed-areas.mjs nor the new test uses it. Impact: a hook-run lane selection computed against the wrong repository, i.e. CI lanes silently skipped. Fix belongs on scripts/changed-areas.mjs (pass `repoScopedEnv(repoRoot)`), not on the test.
searchedFor: grep changed-areas across repo (verify-self.mjs, ci.yml, harness.config.json)

samples.summary: api-keys commands discard the response body, so the SESSION_EXPIRED envelope that routing them through `send()` newly makes reachable is never surfaced
samples.evidence: Routing the API-key endpoints through `sendJson`→`send` (http-client.ts:179-196) means a JWT session that cannot be refreshed now returns `{ ok:false, status:401, data:{ error:{ code:'SESSION_EXPIRED', … } } }` (http-client.ts:190-192) — a shape these endpoints could never produce before. The three callers were updated only to `throw httpError(res.status)` (api-keys.ts:19, :33, :47) and never look at `res.data`, so the machine-readable `SESSION_EXPIRED` code is replaced by a generic `AUTH_ERROR` envelope. Every other command that can receive a backend error body prints it verbatim (e.g. docs.ts:196-203). Exit code is right (2); the `code` an agent branches on is not.

samples.summary: The published user documentation still describes the old CLI surface: no `--allow-unbound-callback`, no exit-code classes
samples.evidence: packages/cli/README.md:30 and docs/design/cli.md:206 both document the new `--allow-unbound-callback` escape hatch (and login.ts:453-470 deliberately relies on the flag being discoverable only in `--help` and the README). The VitePress site's CLI page documents `login` (packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:22,30) and the global flag table (:106-111) but mentions neither the new flag nor the `1` = user / `2` = system exit contract; its only exit-code statement is the unrelated `:263`. Consumer doc left describing the old contract.

samples.summary: Local I/O faults still return the hardcoded user-error code while the rest of the CLI moved to status-derived classes
samples.evidence: `runFilesUpload` now classifies HTTP failures with `exitCodeForStatus` (upload.ts:222) but a genuine environment fault — `FILE_READ_FAILED` at upload.ts:205-212 (EISDIR, permission denied) — still returns `{ exitCode: 1 }`, as do notes/import.ts:132, docs/import.ts:139 and slides/import.ts:164 for their `NOT_A_TTY`/read paths. Under the new contract (`errors.ts:1-10`: `2` = system error, `1` = something the caller can retype) an unreadable file arguably belongs in the system class; at minimum the split between the two is now decided differently in adjacent branches of the same function.

samples.summary: Process-wide env mutation at module scope runs after the module under test is imported and bypasses the repo's own git-env helpers
samples.evidence: scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs:50 deletes `GIT_*` from the shared `process.env` in the module body, which ES module semantics evaluate *after* `import … from "../changed-areas.mjs"` (line 26) has already run that module. It also duplicates, rather than uses, `fixtureGitEnv`/`repoScopedEnv` (scripts/agent/git-env.mjs:102,120) which every other git-touching script in scripts/ uses, and none of the ~8 `execFileSync("git", …, { cwd })` sites in this file (e.g. :80, :374, :408, :597) pass an `env`, so the protection is entirely dependent on that one global side effect surviving future edits.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: scripts/changed-areas.mjs spawns git in two places — the `git()` helper in resolveRefs (255-259) and changedPaths (350-354) — with only `cwd: repoRoot` and no `env`, so both inherit process.env including any GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE git exports to hooks. The repo's canonical scoping helpers exist and are exported (scripts/agent/git-env.mjs:102 repoScopedEnv, :120 fixtureGitEnv, :138-148 readHeadSha showing the intended `env: repoScopedEnv(root)` usage), but changed-areas.mjs imports none of them. I searched the whole chain for the scrub elsewhere and found none: .githooks/pre-push:1-2 is a bare `exec pnpm verify:self`; package.json:22 has no env wrapper; scripts/verify-self.mjs has no env handling at all (only the import at :3 and a comment at :546) and calls resolveChangedAreas() at :602 with default process.env; a repo-wide grep for GIT_DIR/repoScopedEnv/`delete process.env`/`env -u`/`unset GIT` outside .trusted turns up scrubbing only in test files. scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs:33-51 does delete every GIT_* at module scope and its comment (44-48) explicitly states this is what makes the module-under-test's in-process git spawns respect the fixture — i.e. the protection is test-process-only. In-lane for blast radius: an invariant enforced elsewhere in the harness (repo-scoped git reads, which verify-self.mjs's HEAD guard depends on via readHeadSha) is violated by a module on the same pre-push entry path, so hook-run lane selection can answer about whatever GIT_DIR names rather than repoRoot. No counterexample found.
